chapter: Fletcher Henderson and forming his own band
title: Arranging for Fletcher Henderson
summary: Carter recalls his arrangements for Henderson in 1928-29 and wonders whether Henderson's Stomp was Fletcher's own.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Uh huh. Well, we're coming down now to about '30, '31, in there and you arranged -- you had been an Alto instrumentalist, a trumpet player; you had even had your own band for a little while, and now I think comes a series of movements in and out of several bands -- Fletcher Henderson, Chick Webb, back to Fletcher Henderson. Now, I wanted to ask you about your -- about the days with Fletcher Henderson.

You had already begun to arrange as early as 1927, with Charlie Johnson and your arrangements were played and recorded. Now, you did some arrangements then, for Fletcher Henderson at that time, too, in this period when you joined him?
I don't know how early. Was it around '28 or something?
Right ^29, something like that.
You did arrange for them. Did you do any arrangements for him at a time when you were not playing in the band?
I don't remember; I don't think so.

And you joined him for a longer period somewhat later, I think, after that first session with him, you had -- or after that first period with him, you had a longer period. Now in that period, you did more arranging, I think, than in the earlier one.
I guess I did.
And did Fletcher himself do much arranging for his own band at that time?
I don't remember playing any Fletcher arrangements at that time.
Uh huh.
And it may be just a matter of my faulty memory.
Right. Who were some ...
You know, I just remembered something. There was a thing called Henderson's Stomp, and I'm wondering if Fletcher didn't do that?
Yes.
You know, it went, (SINGS) ba ba ba ba ba da da dum ...
Yes.
Yeah, you know? That might -- if this should prove to be ... because I think I played that.
Uh huh.
I think I played that. I don't think
that was later. And that would certainly belie my statement that he didn't, you know, arrange ...
Couldn't it have been Horace, because Horace also did arrangements.
I don't know.
Well, we could look into that.
Yeah. That could be interesting.
